title: A strong mission, [mute:too many doors.] Making ne-arc.org work for families, donors and parcels.
lede: A review of the Northeast Arc homepage and its key journeys: getting support, donating, and shopping at parcels, on desktop and mobile.

summary.heading: The site explains who Northeast Arc is. It does not tell each visitor what to do next.
summary.intro: Northeast Arc serves three very different audiences from one homepage: families looking for help, donors and supporters, and job seekers. Today they all meet a nine slide carousel, a long services grid and a footer full of links. [risk:On phones the Donate button disappears entirely until the footer]. parcels, the organisation's own social enterprise, [risk:is slide five of nine]. The recommendations below give each audience a clear path and use the homepage's traffic to [gain:lift parcels sales].

kpis.label: Critical issues blocking sales or goals
Estimated increase in visitors sent to the parcels store

takeaways.label: The core problem
takeaways.text: There is [risk:no single primary action.] Nine rotating slides compete for attention, so families, donors and shoppers all have to hunt.

takeaways.label: The biggest lever
takeaways.text: On mobile, [key:Donate is hidden] in the menu and only visible in the footer, about 7,100px down the page.

takeaways.label: The parcels link
takeaways.text: The homepage reaches far more people than the store. A [key:permanent parcels module] would turn existing supporters into gift buyers.

strengths.heading: What is already working
strengths.intro: These are worth protecting in any redesign.

items.title: Human, credible story
items.text: Founded by parents in 1954, the origin story is moving and well written, and photos show real people served.

items.title: Social proof
items.text: Awards (Top Workplace, Top Women-Led Businesses) and partner logos (Cummings, BCBS Foundation, ECCF) build trust.

items.title: Clear intake contact
items.text: A referral email and phone number sit right above the services, so families have a direct line.

items.title: Accessibility intent
items.text: An accessibility widget and a language switcher are present on every page.

items.title: Well described services
items.text: Seven service areas each have a short, plain language summary and a Learn more link.

items.title: Strong impact numbers
items.text: 10,000+ people, 190+ communities and 1,100+ employees are memorable proof of scale.

findings.heading: Issues, evidence and fixes
findings.intro: Each finding shows the live screen we captured, the problem marked in orange, what to change, and the result you can expect. Ordered by business impact.

items.title: On mobile, the Donate button is hidden until the footer, about 7,100px down

shots.alt: Mobile header: social icons and search, no Donate
shots.caption: Mobile header: social icons and search, no Donate

shots.alt: Seven full width service tiles before the footer
shots.caption: Seven full width service tiles before the footer

items.why: Most nonprofit website traffic now comes from phones, often from social posts. If supporters cannot see how to give within a thumb's reach, many will not open a menu to look for it.
found: On desktop, Donate is a clear purple button in the header. On a 375px phone it is [risk:folded into the MENU].
The first Donate link visible without opening the menu is in the footer, [key:about 7,100px down a 7,850px page].
[key:The top 160px] of the phone screen is used by social icons, Careers, News, Contact and a search box.
recommendations: Keep a [fix:Donate] button visible in the mobile header next to MENU, or add a slim sticky "Donate" bar at the bottom.
[fix:Move social icons and search into the menu] on mobile to give the first screen back to content.
Use the same purple button style everywhere so Donate is instantly recognisable.

impact.label: mobile visits to the donation page

items.title: A nine slide auto carousel replaces a clear headline and primary action

shots.alt: First slide on load: a photo with no message or button
shots.caption: First slide on load: a photo with no message or button

shots.alt: Caption box covers the slide dots and clips "Read more"
shots.caption: Caption box covers the slide dots and clips "Read more"

items.why: Carousels spread attention thin; most visitors only ever see the first slide. When that slide carries no message, the homepage's most valuable space says nothing.
found: The hero [key:rotates nine slides]: awards, jobs, parcels, legacy giving, a playground, mental health training and more.
On load, the first slide shows a photo with [risk:no headline or button for several seconds]; on mobile the caption area is blank white.
The caption panel overlaps the slide indicators, and the "Read more" link is [risk:cut off by the decorative wave].
recommendations: Replace the carousel with a [fix:static hero]: "Lifelong support for people with disabilities and autism" plus three buttons: [fix:Get support, Donate, Shop parcels].
Move news, awards and events into a "What's happening" row of three cards below.
If a carousel stays, stop autoplay, show the caption on load and keep controls clear of the text.

impact.label: clicks from the homepage to key pages

items.title: parcels, the organisation's own store, is buried as slide 5 of 9 and a third level menu item

shots.alt: The homepage ends without any shop or gift module
shots.caption: The homepage ends without any shop or gift module

items.why: ne-arc.org reaches families, staff, donors and partners who already care about the mission, the warmest possible audience for parcels. Today almost none of that attention is passed to the store.
found: The only homepage path to parcels is [key:the fifth carousel slide] ("Visit parcels at the Liberty Tree Mall") and About Us > Innovative Businesses > parcels.
The parcels page on ne-arc.org then links out with one "Shop Online Now" button.
There is no product, gift guide or holiday shopping message [risk:anywhere on the homepage in November].
recommendations: Add a permanent [fix:"Shop with purpose"] band on the homepage with 4 featured products pulled from parcelsgifts.com and a "Shop holiday gifts" button.
Add [fix:Shop parcels] as a top level menu item (with an external link icon).
Promote parcels in the mailing list and on the Thank you page after a donation.

impact.label: parcels online orders from ne-arc.org visitors

items.title: The donation page has no story, no impact framing and no "why give now"

shots.alt: The emotive copy lives on the homepage, not on the donation page
shots.caption: The emotive copy lives on the homepage, not on the donation page

items.why: Donors give to outcomes, not to forms. A short story and concrete impact amounts typically raise both completion rate and average gift.
found: Apart from the embedded donation form, [risk:the page copy is a single link]: "Click Here For More Ways To Give".
[risk:No headline, photo, impact examples] ("$50 funds..."), monthly giving prompt or tax deductible note in the page content.
Header Donate and footer Donate [risk:point to different pages] (/donate-online-to-northeast-arc/ vs /get-involved/donate/).
recommendations: Add a headline and photo above the form, plus 3 impact tiers: [fix:$50, $150, $500] with what each achieves.
Default to [fix:monthly giving] with a one time option; add "Your gift is tax deductible" and a charity rating badge if available.
Point every Donate link to the same page and add a parcels gift suggestion on the Thank you screen.

items.title: Families looking for help must decode service names; there is no "Get support" path

shots.alt: Intake details are one line of small text above the grid
shots.caption: Intake details are one line of small text above the grid

shots.alt: Seven tiles in a three column grid leave one orphan tile
shots.caption: Seven tiles in a three column grid leave one orphan tile

items.why: A parent arriving after a diagnosis is often stressed and unfamiliar with the jargon. Guiding them by age or need shortens the path to an intake call.
found: Help seekers [risk:must know terms such as] "Day Habilitation", "Specialty ABA" or "LTSS" to find the right service.
The referral email and phone appear as one line of text, [risk:easy to miss].

The services grid has 7 tiles in 3 columns, leaving Clinical Services alone with empty space on both sides; the grid is also coded twice (once per screen size), so [risk:screen readers hear every heading twice].
recommendations: Add a [fix:"Find support for..."] selector: Infant or toddler, School age child, Adult, Family or caregiver.
Turn the intake line into a prominent card with a "Request a call back" form.
Rebalance the grid (4 + 4 with a "Find support" tile) and remove the duplicate markup.

impact.label: time to first contact for families

items.title: Mobile first screen: utility bar and a blank caption area push content down

shots.alt: On load, a large blank area sits under the photo
shots.caption: On load, a large blank area sits under the photo

shots.alt: After a few seconds the caption appears
shots.caption: After a few seconds the caption appears

items.why: Blank space during load looks broken, and very long pages hide the footer contact details and Donate link.
found: On first load the space below the hero photo is [risk:blank white until the slider script runs].
The page is [key:about 7,850px tall on a phone], with services stacked as seven full screen tiles.
recommendations: [fix:Render the caption in HTML on load] instead of waiting for the slider script.
Show services as a compact two column icon grid on mobile.

impact.label: scroll depth to contact and Donate

items.title: Footer headings collide and text breaks mid word

shots.alt: "HEADQUARTERS QUICK LINKS" run together; "Massachuset ts" and "info@ne- arc.org" break
shots.caption: "HEADQUARTERS QUICK LINKS" run together; "Massachuset ts" and "info@ne- arc.org" break

items.why: Small layout faults in the footer, where people look for contact details, chip away at the organisation's credibility.
found: The Headquarters and Quick Links headings touch, [risk:reading as one heading].
Narrow columns break "Massachusetts" and the email address across lines.
The upcoming event link reads "View Upcoming Event $" [risk:with a stray dollar sign].
recommendations: Use a [fix:4 column grid with fixed gutters]; let long words wrap normally and keep the email on one line.
Fix the event link label.

items.title: "Join our mailing list" sends people to another page instead of capturing the email

shots.alt: The Sign up button links to the Get Involved page
shots.caption: The Sign up button links to the Get Involved page

items.why: Every extra click loses subscribers. The mailing list is the cheapest channel for donations, events and parcels promotions.
found: The large Sign up button opens /get-involved/ [risk:rather than showing an email field].
[key:Impact numbers differ across properties]: 10,000+ people and 190+ towns here, 12,000 people and nearly 200 communities on parcelsgifts.com.
recommendations: Put an [fix:email field and button directly in the band]; offer interests (Donor news, Family resources, parcels gifts).
Align impact numbers across ne-arc.org and parcelsgifts.com.

items.title: A heavy homepage, and inner pages that refused our test browser
items.why: Slow pages lose mobile visitors, and an over strict security rule can silently block donors and families, particularly on shared networks, VPNs or privacy browsers.
found: The homepage made [key:193 requests and transferred about 14 MB], with 156 script tags; full load took about 3.3 seconds on a fast connection.
After the homepage loaded, every inner page we opened in our test browser (About, Services, Donate) [risk:returned "403 Forbidden"] from the server.
The same pages loaded when fetched by a different client, which suggests a firewall or bot rule that [risk:may also block some real visitors].
recommendations: [fix:Audit plugins and scripts] (events, Instagram, sliders, translation) and remove what is not used on the homepage.
Serve images as WebP at display size; enable caching and a CDN.
[fix:Ask the hosting provider to review WAF and rate limit rules] and check server logs for legitimate visitors receiving 403 errors.

impact.heading: What these fixes are worth
impact.intro: Ranges are based on nonprofit and e-commerce benchmarks and our experience. They are directional; validate with Google Analytics and your donation platform reports.

rows.measure: GA4: page views of the donation page from mobile
Referral emails, calls and form submissions
Square: sessions referred by ne-arc.org (UTM tagged)

scenario.note: Illustrative model with assumed traffic, not Northeast Arc data. Supporters arriving from ne-arc.org are mission aware, so they usually convert better than average shop visitors; this model is deliberately conservative. Tag all parcels links with UTM parameters to measure the real effect.

roadmap.heading: A 90 day plan, quick wins first
roadmap.intro: Sequenced so the cheapest, highest impact fixes ship in the first two weeks and pay for the rest.

phases.title: Quick wins
items: Visible Donate button in the mobile header
Shop parcels in the main menu, UTM tagged
Inline mailing list field
Footer fixes and one Donate destination
Hosting review of 403 / WAF rules

phases.title: Clear paths
items: Static hero with Get support, Donate, Shop parcels
"Shop with purpose" homepage band
Donation page story and impact tiers
Script and image clean up

phases.title: Deeper journeys
items: "Find support for..." selector and call back form
Rebuilt services grid and mobile layout
Monthly giving program and donor thank you journey
Shared impact numbers across both sites

blocks.title: Scope and setup
items: Live review on November 4, 2026 of the homepage on desktop (1024 x 768) and mobile emulation (375 x 812) in Chromium.
The Donate and parcels pages were reviewed from their page source, because the test browser received 403 errors on inner pages.

blocks.title: Frameworks
items: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics and a nonprofit donation journey checklist.
WCAG 2.2 spot checks (heading structure, duplicated content, tap targets).
Page weight and timing from the browser Performance API.

blocks.title: Scoring
items: Each area scored 0 to 100 against the checklist; the overall score is the average.
Severity: Critical blocks a primary goal (donating, getting support), High measurably reduces it, Medium and Low affect trust and polish.

blocks.title: Limitations
items: No access to analytics or donation data, so impact ranges are estimates.
Interior service pages could not be inspected visually; a follow up review is recommended once access rules are confirmed.
